_schema.purpose: Shared CLI parity fixture. Both drivers -- gwz-py and gwz-cli -- read this file and assert against it; neither restates these cases inline. Add a case here, not in a driver's test module.
_schema.stability: Keys and case ids are stable. Append cases; do not renumber, rename or reorder existing ones. A case a driver cannot express is scoped with `drivers`, never deleted.
_schema.coordination: UNRESOLVED as of 2026-09-06: lanes CP and CR each built the shared local-family fixture in their own repo, to different schemas. This file is CP's (design section 7 rows in `message_cases`/`message_refusals`); gwz-cli/tests/fixtures/cli_parity/local_family_cases.json is CR's, with `accept`/`reject` and a nested `request` object instead of dotted paths. The two carry the same design rows and, after this revision, the same expected values -- only the addressing and the refusal-needle convention differ. One of them should win; until the lane owner picks, treat the row VALUES here as authoritative and the schema as provisional.

argv_lists.what: Each entry is a bare argv list: no program name, no shell quoting.
argv_lists.accept: parses and validates in both drivers
argv_lists.parse_reject: rejected by the argument parser itself
argv_lists.semantic_reject: parses, then refused by validation or the command handler before any core call
argv_lists.rust_accept: flag spellings that originate in the Rust CLI and must also parse in the Python CLI
argv_lists.rust_version: argv that prints a version and exits 0

message_cases.what: One entry per design section 7 'CLI -> live message' row (dev-docs/GwzLocalCloneDesign.md, revision 9), plus the section 4 `--from` selector. Each pins the command line a person types, the protocol message it must build, and the field values that message must carry. Nothing here reaches core: the assertion is on the encoded request.
message_cases.design_row: the design table cell this case pins, verbatim
message_cases.argv: argv without the program name, byte-identical to the design's command line
message_cases.message: the generated request message's type name
message_cases.fields: dotted paths from the request root to the expected value. A path resolves through an absent (null) intermediate to null, so `meta.policy.remote` is null when the request carries no policy object at all. Enum values are the protocol enum's own name in snake_case (`verbatim`, `ff_only`, `start`); everything else is literal JSON.
message_cases.drivers: optional; which drivers accept this spelling. Default is both: ["python", "rust"].
message_cases.core_refuses: optional; the GwzErrorCode core answers for this request. The CLI still encodes and sends it -- the key records that the refusal is core's, not the CLI's.

message_refusals.what: Command lines a driver must refuse before encoding any request. `refused_by` says whose refusal it is.
message_refusals.refused_by: `cli` -- the driver refuses before any core call
message_refusals.message_contains: substrings the refusal message contains. Every listed substring must appear; the wording around them differs per driver, so keep these short.

message_cases.design_row: gwz clone --local --name A ../gwz-dev-A (--verbatim is the default, spelled out)

message_cases.note: An absent dest is core's default, not a CLI-side path join.

message_cases.design_row: -b is accepted with --bare as well as --clean (design section 4.3)
Copy source is cwd (or --from <name|path>) (design section 4; wire field copy_source, section 7 and section 11 item 11)
message_cases.note: `from` is a keyword in both generated languages, so the wire field is copy_source (tag 6). The CLI does not decide whether the token is a family name or a path -- core resolves it.

message_cases.design_row: v0 local create refuses an unsupported dry-run in core (design section 6.2)
message_cases.note: The local-family verbs pass --dry-run through for core to refuse; only the URL clone keeps its own CLI-side refusal (see message_refusals/url-clone-dry-run).

The split is on ',' and nothing else: no trimming, no case folding, no normalization. A deletion waiver is the operator's authorization token; rewriting it before encoding would make the CLI answer for a vocabulary that belongs to core. Core refuses ' open-merge' as an unknown hazard, which is the correct answer to what was actually typed.
The hazard vocabulary is core's. The CLI refuses only the shapes that would be misread on the wire -- a force naming nothing, or an empty element.

message_cases.design_row: the family verbs pass --dry-run through for core to refuse

message_cases.note: pull binds the name through OperationPolicy.remote, not a request field. Core resolves a ready family name first and falls back to a git remote.
Identical encoding to the family row: `origin` is reserved as a family name, so this reaches the git remote and never UnknownLocal.
For merge, --remote is family-only: a MergeRequest field, never OperationPolicy.remote. HEAD per paired member.

message_cases.design_row: gwz merge --remote origin -> UnknownLocal (family-only; reserved / not a member)
message_cases.note: merge --remote has no git-remote fallback, so the CLI encodes the name unchanged and core answers unknown_local (62) with the state detail in the message. Pull and push keep missing_remote for their neither case.

message_cases.design_row: gwz merge A -> git ref `A`, not a family name
an invalid or unsupported family start refuses in core (design section 6.2)
message_cases.note: merge --dry-run is a supported merge shape; the family selector does not add a CLI-side refusal to it.

PushRequest.remote carries the token: a ready family row wins, an absent row falls back to a git remote. Whether the token ALSO stays in OperationPolicy.remote is a live divergence -- see push-remote-python-clears-the-policy-binding.

DIVERGENCE, unresolved: gwz-py moves --remote out of the policy meta into PushRequest.remote, so meta.policy.remote is absent; gwz-cli sets PushRequest.remote and leaves the same token in OperationPolicy.remote. The same argv therefore encodes different bytes. Design section 7 names only PushRequest.remote for push and only meta.policy.remote for pull, so it does not settle which is right. Scoped to python until a ruling; do not read this row as the shared contract.

message_refusals.note: DIVERGENCE, unresolved: gwz-py refuses an empty --name before encoding; gwz-cli encodes name="" and lets core answer, on the stated principle that core owns name validity and the CLI refuses only shapes that would be MISREAD on the wire -- an empty name is a distinct invalid value, not an absent one. Both readings are defensible; gwz-py's costs nothing and reaches the operator sooner. Scoped to python until a ruling.
An empty copy_source is not `the cwd workspace`: the absent field means that. Encoding an empty string would ask core to resolve a nameless source.
--name, --verbatim, --clean, --bare, -b and --from all mean nothing without --local; each refuses the same way.
The URL clone keeps its own pre-existing CLI-side --dry-run refusal. The local-family verbs do not copy it: they pass --dry-run through for core to refuse (see the *-dry-run message_cases).
An empty force_hazards list is `no force`, so encoding one for a --force invocation would invert the operator's authorization.

The global --force before the verb is the same refusal. Design section 11 item 15: the Rust CLI cannot add a subcommand --force beside the global one, so it parses the hazard list as operands of the global flag; every command line in sections 5 and 8 stays byte-identical.

gwz-cli distinguishes an empty list from an empty element and says `must not contain an empty hazard name`; gwz-py cannot -- argparse gives a bare --force and --force "" the same value -- so it answers both with one message. Same refusal, different wording, hence the short needle.

Refused at the CLI in both drivers, although design section 7 also assigns it to core (`core rejects unknown hazards and keep+force`). Detaching and waiving loss are opposite intents; the CLI refuses the contradiction before it costs a family lock, and core keeps its own check for non-CLI callers.
local_source_name is start-only; --continue, --abort, --status and --gc each refuse the same way.
